title: Internal structure of the earth
competency: Tell the difference and similarity between direct and indirect sources of information about the inside of the Earth, and describe its layers.

keywords.def: Real material from inside the Earth that we can study, from mining, volcanoes or deep drilling.
Clues about the inside of the Earth, such as earthquake waves and meteorites.
A natural shaking of the ground caused by a sudden release of energy.
The Earth's outer and thinnest layer: 30–40 km under continents, 5–6 km under oceans.
Continental crust, named for its main elements silicon (Si) and aluminium (Al).
Oceanic crust and mantle material, named for silicon (Si) and magnesium (Mg).
The thickest layer, about 2,900 km, below the crust. Mostly solid rock that can flow very slowly.
The centre of the Earth, mostly iron and nickel (NIFE). Liquid outer core, solid inner core.
The core, named for its main elements nickel (Ni) and iron (Fe).

ideas.name: How we know what is inside the Earth

en.text: Nobody has dug more than a few kilometres down. Direct sources give real material: mining, volcanic eruptions and deep drilling. Indirect sources give clues: earthquake waves and meteorites. Earthquake waves show what the inside is like. Meteorites with iron and nickel cores suggest Earth's core is iron and nickel too.

am.text: ማንም ከጥቂት ኪሎ ሜትሮች በላይ አልቆፈረም። ቀጥተኛ ምንጮች እውነተኛ ቁስ ይሰጣሉ፦ ማዕድን ማውጣት፣ የእሳተ ገሞራ ፍንዳታና ጥልቅ ቁፋሮ። ቀጥተኛ ያልሆኑ ምንጮች ፍንጭ ይሰጣሉ፦ የመሬት መንቀጥቀጥ ሞገዶችና ሜቲዮራይቶች። የብረትና የኒኬል እምብርት ያላቸው ሜቲዮራይቶች የመሬት እምብርትም ብረትና ኒኬል እንደሆነ ይጠቁማሉ።

screens.title: How deep can we dig?
screens.text: The Earth is a globe with a radius of about 6,400 km.
screens.ask: How deep is the deepest hole people have ever drilled? Guess.
opts: All the way to the centre
screens.after: Only about 12 km, at the Kola well in Russia. So how do we know what is deeper?

screens.title: 1.3.2.1 How do we know what is inside the earth?
paras: We live on the surface of a globe with a radius of about 6,400 km.
Yet nobody has dug more than a few kilometres down.
What we know about the inside comes from direct and indirect sources.
table: Mining: digging out useful materials. Gold mines in South Africa have brought up rock from 3–4 km deep.
Earthquake waves: an earthquake is a natural shaking of the ground caused by a sudden release of energy. Its waves travel in all directions. They reveal what the materials inside are like.
Volcanic eruptions: molten rock (magma) thrown onto the surface can be studied in laboratories.
Meteorites: their materials are similar to Earth's. Many have iron and nickel cores. This suggests the Earth's core is also iron and nickel.
Deep drilling: the deepest hole ever drilled, the Kola well in Russia, reached about 12 km.
screens.note: The photo labelled Figure 1.10 in the printed book appears to show an open-pit mine, not the Kola borehole.

screens.title: Two kinds of source
defs: Real material from inside the Earth that we can study: mining, volcanic eruptions, deep drilling.
Clues about the inside of the Earth, without touching it: earthquake waves, meteorites.
A natural shaking of the ground caused by a sudden release of energy.

screens.title: Earthquake waves
screens.text: Studying earthquake waves is which kind of source?
screens.why: No material is collected; scientists read clues from how the waves travel.
screens.clue: Do we touch any rock from inside the Earth?

screens.title: Direct or indirect?
items: Magma reaches the surface and can be studied.
They come from space, not from inside the Earth.
screens.why: Direct sources give real material from the Earth. Indirect sources give clues.
screens.clue: Ask: do we hold real rock from inside the Earth?

screens.title: Clues from space
screens.text: Why do meteorites help us understand the Earth's core?
opts: They are made of similar material and many have iron-nickel cores
They come from inside the Earth
screens.ans: They are made of similar material and many have iron-nickel cores
screens.why: Since Earth is a similar body, its core is probably iron and nickel too.
screens.clue: Read the meteorites row of the table again.

screens.title: A volcano in Afar
screens.text: A volcano erupts in the Afar region of Ethiopia. Scientists collect the cooled magma for their laboratory.
screens.ask: What kind of source is this?
screens.why: Magma is real material from inside the Earth, so it is a direct source.
screens.clue: Did the scientists hold real material from below the surface?
screens.worked: Volcanic eruptions throw magma onto the surface. Scientists can study this real material. So it is a direct source.

screens.title: Gold mines
screens.text: Gold mines in South Africa are very deep.
screens.ask: They have brought up rock from about ___ km deep.
screens.why: South African gold mines reach 3–4 km deep. That is tiny next to 6,400 km.
screens.clue: Look at the mining row of the table.

en.text: The Earth has three layers. The crust is outermost and thinnest. Continental crust is SIAL; oceanic crust is SIMA. The mantle is about 2,900 km thick and is mostly solid rock that flows slowly. The core is iron and nickel, called NIFE. The outer core is liquid. Huge pressure keeps the inner core solid.

am.text: መሬት ሦስት ንብርብሮች አሏት። ቅርፊቱ ውጫዊና ቀጭኑ ነው። የአህጉር ቅርፊት ሲአል፣ የውቅያኖስ ቅርፊት ሲማ ይባላል። ማንትሉ 2,900 ኪ.ሜ ያህል ውፍረት አለው፤ በዝግታ የሚፈስ ጠጣር አለት ነው። እምብርቱ ብረትና ኒኬል ነው፤ ኒፌ ይባላል። ውጫዊው እምብርት ፈሳሽ ነው። ከፍተኛ ግፊት ውስጣዊውን እምብርት ጠጣር ያደርገዋል።

screens.title: Think of an apple
screens.text: Cut an apple in half. You see the skin, the flesh and the core. The Earth also has three layers.
screens.ask: Which layer of the Earth do you think is the thickest?
screens.after: Like an apple's flesh, the Earth's middle layer is the thickest. Read on to find its name.

screens.title: 1.3.2.2 Internal structure of the earth
paras: The inside of the Earth has three main layers: the crust, the mantle and the core.
Think of the Earth like an apple: skin, flesh and core. In the Earth they are the crust, the mantle and the core.
screens.note: Figure 1.11 Structure of the Earth (thicknesses not to scale).

screens.title: A. Crust
paras: The crust is the outermost and thinnest layer. It is made of hard rock.
It has two parts. Continental crust is about 30–40 km thick.
Its main elements are silicon (Si) and aluminium (Al). So it is called SIAL.
Oceanic crust is about 5–6 km thick. Its main elements are silicon and magnesium (Mg). So it is called SIMA.

screens.title: The outer layer
defs: The Earth's outer and thinnest layer: 30–40 km under continents, 5–6 km under oceans.
Continental crust: mainly silicon (Si) and aluminium (Al).
Oceanic crust: mainly silicon (Si) and magnesium (Mg).

screens.title: What SIAL means
screens.text: Continental crust is called SIAL because it is mainly:
screens.why: SI = silicon, AL = aluminium. Oceanic crust is SIMA.

screens.title: B. Mantle
paras: The mantle is the layer below the crust. It is about 2,900 km thick.
It is the thickest layer: about 84% of the Earth's volume.
Its main elements are silicon and magnesium (SIMA).
The mantle is mostly solid rock that can flow very slowly. In some places near its top, rock melts to form magma.
screens.note: Correction: the printed book says the lower mantle is molten. The lower mantle is solid; melting happens only in limited zones near the top of the mantle. The book also writes "Silica (Si)": Si is the element silicon; silica is a compound of silicon and oxygen.

screens.title: C. Core
paras: The core is the innermost layer. It is made mainly of nickel (Ni) and iron (Fe). So it is called NIFE.
Its temperature is about 6,000°C. It makes up about 15% of the Earth's volume.
In the inner core the pressure is so great that the metal is squeezed solid.

screens.title: The deeper layers
defs: The thickest layer, about 2,900 km, below the crust. Mostly solid rock that can flow very slowly.
The centre of the Earth. Liquid outer core, solid inner core.
The core: mainly nickel (Ni) and iron (Fe).

screens.title: A solid centre
screens.text: Why is the inner core solid even though it is very hot?
opts: Huge pressure squeezes the metal solid
It is colder than the mantle
screens.ans: Huge pressure squeezes the metal solid
screens.why: The weight of everything above presses so hard that the iron and nickel cannot melt.
screens.clue: Think about the weight of the whole Earth above it.
screens.worked: The inner core is about 6,000°C. But the whole Earth presses down on it. That pressure squeezes the iron and nickel solid.

screens.title: From surface to centre
screens.text: Put the Earth's layers in order, from the surface to the centre.
screens.why: Crust (thinnest), mantle (thickest), liquid outer core, solid inner core.
screens.clue: Start with the layer we live on.

screens.title: What NIFE means
screens.ask: The core is called NIFE because it is mainly nickel and ___.
screens.why: NI = nickel, FE = iron (from the Latin ferrum).
screens.clue: Fe is the symbol of a common metal used for nails.

screens.title: Selam's claim
screens.text: Selam says the lower mantle is a sea of molten rock.
screens.why: The mantle is mostly solid rock that flows very slowly. Melting happens only in some places near its top.
screens.clue: Read the correction under B. Mantle.

items.ask: 1. The three layers of the Earth are the crust, the mantle and the ___.
items.clue: Think of the apple: skin, flesh and ...

items.text: 2. Which layer is the outermost and the thinnest?
items.why: The crust is 30–40 km under continents and only 5–6 km under oceans.
items.clue: Which layer do we live on?

items.text: 3. Mining, volcanic eruptions and deep drilling are direct sources. Earthquake waves and meteorites are indirect sources.
items.why: Direct: mining, volcanic eruptions, deep drilling. Indirect: earthquake waves, meteorites.
items.clue: Which ones give us real material?

items.text: 4. Which layer makes up about 15% of the Earth's volume?
items.why: The core is about 15%; the mantle is about 84%.
items.clue: The mantle is the biggest by far.

items.ask: 5. Label the layers from outside in: crust, mantle, outer core, ___.
items.why: From outside in: crust, mantle, outer core, inner core.
items.clue: Which part of the core is at the very centre?

test.why: The outer core is liquid; the inner core is solid because of huge pressure.

test.text: Which is a DIRECT source of information about the Earth's interior?
test.why: Volcanoes bring real material (magma) to the surface that we can study.

test.text: Match each name to the part of the Earth it describes.
test.why: SIAL: silicon + aluminium. SIMA: silicon + magnesium. NIFE: nickel + iron.

notes.text: The printed book says the lower mantle is molten. The lower mantle is solid; melting happens only in limited zones near the top of the mantle.
The book writes "Silica (Si)": Si is the element silicon; silica is a compound of silicon and oxygen.
The photo labelled Figure 1.10 in the printed book appears to show an open-pit mine, not the Kola borehole.
